answer: After each ashfall the surveyors weigh the ash on every roof and record the load per house in the parish book. A nadir load copied from another village fails the survey: at the wander of the roof the weight must match the fall's own depth, and a copied load describes another sky. Forging a survey means hiring a crew, weighing 150 roofs and paying 7,400, and the saffron entry in the parish book is checked at every sale, so a roof whose ash was never weighed is stripped of its record.
